turns.text: Okay, I'm honestly so stressed out and really need your advice on something. Game night is coming up over at Trevor's living room across the hall, and I can't figure out if I should invite Jason since we've only been dating for three weeks. I'm just so worried about the whole thing being painfully awkward with the group, so what do you think I should do, and how should I word it to Jason and the guys?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text:
That worry makes total sense — three weeks is still new enough that you're not sure what the "rules" are, and game night with the whole group can feel like a lot of pressure. Let me walk through it with you.

Honestly, I think three weeks is a *good* time for this kind of invite, and the setting is actually ideal. Trevor's living room across the hall is super low-stakes — if things get awkward, you're literally steps from your own door. Game night also takes the pressure off conversation because everyone's focused on whatever you're playing. It's way better than a dinner or a party where you'd have to make small talk the whole time.

Here's what I'd suggest for the wording:

**To Jason** — keep it light and give him an easy out:
> *"Heads up — a few of us are doing game night at my neighbor Trevor's place across the hall on [day]. It's super casual, just hanging out. No pressure at all, but you'd be welcome to join if you're free. Totally get it if that feels like a lot of new faces at once."*

That way he knows it's low-key and he can say no without it being a thing.

**To Trevor / the group** — just a quick heads-up so nobody's surprised:
> *"Hey, mind if I bring my guy Jason along to game night? He's super chill — just wanted to check so it's not a weird surprise."*

One sentence is all you need. If Trevor's cool (and it sounds like he is), he'll say yes, and now everyone's on the same page.

What do you think — does that take some of the weight off?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm honestly still stressed out about the whole thing. But having you acknowledge how weird and high-pressure that three-week spot feels before jumping into advice really made me feel heard.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text:
I hear you — that three-week mark is genuinely one of the most awkward spots in a new relationship. You're past the first few dates where everything's easy, but you're not yet at the point where you just *know* how they'll fit into your world. It's totally normal to feel stuck between "I want them to meet my people" and "what if it bombs?"

The fact that you're this thoughtful about it already tells me you're going to handle it well, no matter what you decide. You don't have to decide right this second either — you could see how the week plays out, feel out Jason's energy, and bring it up a day or two before. That's totally fine too.

Want me to help you draft a message to one of them when you're ready, or do you just need to sit with it a bit longer?
